commit.message:
feat: add persistent scx phase notifications
add opt-in state mode with a 32-byte v2 ABI
remove CPU worker markers while preserving v1 diagnostic tracing
include focused tests and local validation evidence

-On Linux, `-DLLAMA_SCX_PHASE_TRACE=ON` adds experimental observation markers for the sibling llama-scheduler project. The option defaults to OFF and requires the bundled CPU backend without GPU or BLAS backends. Enable a run with `--scx-phase-run-id UINT64` and explicit `-ngl 0`. Only single-context decoder-only text generation is supported; speculative, multimodal, and embedding modes are rejected.
+On Linux, `-DLLAMA_SCX_PHASE_TRACE=ON` adds experimental markers for the sibling llama-scheduler project. The option defaults to OFF and requires the bundled CPU backend without GPU or BLAS backends. Enabled modes require a nonzero `--scx-phase-run-id UINT64` and explicit `-ngl 0`. Only single-context decoder-only text generation is supported; speculative, multimodal, and embedding modes are rejected.
 
-`llama_scx_decode_begin_v1` and `llama_scx_decode_end_v1` expose the existing call/retry identity, token-origin counts, semantic phase, and requested profile. `ggml_scx_worker_begin_v1` and `ggml_scx_worker_end_v1` mark actual CPU graph work in both OpenMP and native threadpool builds. Worker end occurs before the final graph barrier, and decode end synchronizes pending work. Tracing is diagnostic and changes timing.
+`--scx-phase-mode off|trace|state` selects publication. With neither mode nor run ID, the mode is `off`. A run-ID-only command retains `trace` behavior. Explicit `off` with a run ID is an error; explicit `trace` or `state` requires a trace-enabled build. Validation uses the final argument combination, independently of option order.
 
-These are optional uprobe symbols, not additions to the public libllama API. The fork does not depend on libbpf or update BPF maps itself. In shared builds, use the marker-bearing `libllama-server-impl.so` and `libggml-cpu.so` ELF paths. The matching 80-byte v1 wire layout is in `tools/server/server-scx.h`; the sibling repository documents the loader, bounded maps, manual kernel checkpoint, and validation in `docs/LLAMA_PHASE.md`.
+`trace` retains the 80-byte v1 layout and `llama_scx_decode_begin_v1` / `llama_scx_decode_end_v1` semantics: every decode attempt emits its call/retry identity, token-origin counts, semantic phase, requested profile, and result. Synchronization occurs before begin and end. This is a diagnostic compute interval and changes timing.
+
+`state` calls `llama_scx_phase_set_v2` only when `(phase, active)` changes. The 32-byte layout has four `uint32_t` fields (`version`, `phase`, `active`, `reserved`) at offsets 0, 4, 8, and 12, followed by `uint64_t run_id` and `sequence` at offsets 16 and 24. The version is 2; reserved is zero. IDLE is inactive UNKNOWN; active UNKNOWN is distinct. Sequence increases for each publication and continues across model sleep/resume within a run. Initial idle work emits no event.
+
+State describes the most recently submitted batch until another batch changes its phase or all work becomes inactive. It includes sampling and server processing between decode calls; it does not assert continuous CPU graph execution. Split and retry views use their actual token origins. Successful decode retains state, partial slot completion retains active state, and final completion/cancellation clears it. Fatal errors, escaping exceptions, sleep, model unload, and execution-loop exit clear state after pending work is settled. Publication belongs to the execution loop, including termination cleanup. Pre/post-decode synchronization is retained even when a duplicate state skips publication.
+
+The state is TGID-wide, shared by other threads in the server process. State observations and v1 compute intervals measure different scopes. For 100 consecutive DECODE submissions followed by IDLE, state emits two events; this is a call-count example, not a measured speedup. Do not enable compute-profile diagnostic tracing or verbose logging in timed trials.
+
+CPU worker marker definitions and calls (`ggml_scx_worker_begin_v1` / `ggml_scx_worker_end_v1`) were removed; the final graph barrier and computation are retained. This breaks external tracers attached to those worker symbols. The current sibling loader attaches to server endpoints only, so worker removal removes ordinary calls and does not reduce its attached uprobe hits. Server v1 consumers remain supported.
+
+These are optional uprobe symbols, not additions to the public libllama API. The fork does not depend on libbpf or update BPF maps itself. In shared builds, use the marker-bearing `libllama-server-impl.so` ELF path. Both wire layouts are in `tools/server/server-scx.h`; the sibling repository documents the loader, bounded maps, manual kernel checkpoint, and validation in `docs/LLAMA_PHASE.md`.
+
+Select matching server and loader modes and complete registration before issuing inference. Registration ACK proves attachment; acceptance also requires an applied valid event. Initial state support requires attachment before workload and does not support live reattachment or loader restart recovery. Markers have no delivery ACK; delivery/map failures must fail acceptance. Process death must invalidate consumer registration without relying on a final userspace event. Phase transport does not add a phase-aware scheduling policy.
@@ -0,0 +1,50 @@
+# SCX state notification validation
+
+Candidate date: 2026-10-03. Provider: personal `hsju2021/llama.cpp-fork`, branch `codex/scx-state-notification`, based on `64f4f972a2758d3a730ce78f92aaa05406de40a0`. Scheduler: the paired `llama-scheduler` checkout based on `ffc03c8`. Changes are uncommitted. The M11/M11R provider pin and archived results remain unchanged.
+
+## Implemented scope
+
+- Server modes `off|trace|state`, order-independent option validation, and run-ID-only trace compatibility.
+- Unchanged 80-byte v1 server ABI plus the separate 32-byte v2 state ABI, with size and all field offsets asserted on both sides.
+- Transition suppression, actual submitted-view classification, retained synchronization, and execution-loop cleanup for idle, cancellation, errors, sleep, and exit.
+- Worker endpoint removal with the final graph barrier preserved.
+- Matching scheduler attachment modes, bounded TGID state, run/sequence validation, failure invalidation, process-instance cleanup, and mode-aware reports.
+- A separate candidate acceptance path, including graceful completion and termination during active DECODE, without changing the historical trace provider pin.
+
+Scheduling policy and compute-profile routing are unchanged. The state interval includes sampling and server processing; it is not a v1 compute interval. No performance improvement is claimed.
+
+## Local evidence
+
+Validation runs in an isolated Linux-filesystem source copy under `/home/hs/scx-state-validation`, using WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`. Build tools were extracted into that task directory without system installation or elevated commands. Raw logs, build options, symbol checks, source hashes, and reproduction scripts are retained in `results/scx-state-notification-20261003-local/` in the provider worktree.
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Trace ON, OpenMP ON server build | PASS, clean rebuild |
+| Trace OFF, OpenMP ON server build | PASS |
+| Trace ON, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Trace OFF, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Provider CTest: argument parser, compute profile, state publisher, enabled-build synchronization fixture | 14/14 passed across the four builds |
+| Small CPU ADD/MUL f32 backend checks | 100/100 per build, 400/400 total |
+| ELF symbols in all four builds | PASS: worker symbols absent; v1/v2 server markers present only with trace enabled |
+| Scheduler userspace and BPF compilation with `-Werror` | PASS, compile evidence only |
+| Scheduler Python suites: instrumentation, M11, M11R, state, M10B, validation | 64 cases: 62 passed, 2 skipped |
+| Full scheduler `make check` | Environment gate: selected-child shell test stops because `/sys/kernel/sched_ext/state` is absent |
+| Python/shell syntax and both repository whitespace checks | PASS |
+
+The two skipped cases require separate historical provider checkouts: the legacy socket producer and the fixed M11 semantic source. Current provider ABI and publisher checks run independently in the C++ fixtures. The shell gate expects a native sched_ext state file; the WSL launcher reports that the file is missing. It was not bypassed or treated as native success.
+
+The final ELF audit detected an old worker symbol in the initially reused ON/OpenMP build. Preserved source timestamps had allowed an object from the baseline to remain. That variant was rebuilt with `--clean-first`; its tests and symbols were checked again. The other three variants were fresh builds. Final source SHA-256 checks match every changed code/test file to the validated Linux copy.
+
+The BPF compilation uses the external sched-ext x86 `vmlinux-v6.18-rc4-g6146a0f1dfae.h` fixture from scx commit `e37ab1fd7ec09505c33beaefdc128bab2d582660`, and a Linux v6.17 scheduler UAPI fixture. These are recorded compile inputs, not the target kernel's BTF or proof of verifier compatibility.
+
+Executable fixtures exercise production publication, phase reduction, lifecycle guards, synchronization, BPF handlers, map/read failures, run and sequence rejection, active UNKNOWN, real-child pidfd cleanup, exit/update races, and report acceptance. They verify two notifications for 100 repeated DECODE calls followed by IDLE, and five notifications for PREFILL/DECODE/DECODE/MIXED/DECODE/IDLE. Actual server token extraction, slot completion/cancellation, model unload, and loop integration were source-reviewed; model-backed lifecycle runs remain pending.
+
+Registration cleanup also exercises 127 successive process identities, same-PID reuse, and deletion failures. The last inactive state is retained for reporting, then reclaimed when the next registration starts, so completed processes do not fill the bounded map.
+
+## Manual checkpoint
+
+The paired scheduler's `docs/LLAMA_PHASE.md` contains the exact native build and runtime commands. Its `AGENTS.md` requires explicit approval before `sudo` or sched_ext loading. No kernel load, uprobe attachment, SCHED_EXT workload, model inference, or performance trial was executed locally.
+
+On the intended native host, verify the selected Ryzen 5 5600G / 48 GB machine, target BTF/UAPI, actual ELF paths, and build options. Run the old trace acceptance and the new state acceptance separately. The controlled state path requires exactly three applied transitions and sequence 3 for normal completion. The abnormal path adds PREFILL and DECODE from a second request, then requires sequence 5 plus evidence that termination invalidated active DECODE. Zero delivery, per-call DECODE publication, sequence gaps, and diagnostic failures fail acceptance.
+
+Then agree on regression thresholds and run matched trace-disabled, runtime-off, trace, and state timing trials with fixed policy and instrumentation. Keep hit-count diagnostics separate from timed runs and preserve raw SSE grouped events. Live reattachment, resynchronization after loader restart, synchronization removal, and policy changes remain deferred.

+#include "../tools/server/server-scx.h"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <vector>
+
+#define CHECK(condition) do { if (!(condition)) { std::fprintf(stderr, "%s:%d: %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #condition); std::abort(); } } while (0)
+
+struct recorder {
+    server_scx_state_publisher publisher;
+    std::vector<server_scx_state_v2> events;
+
+    bool publish(uint32_t phase) {
+        return publisher.publish(42, phase, true, [this](const server_scx_state_v2 * event) { events.push_back(*event); });
+    }
+    bool reconcile(bool processing) {
+        return publisher.reconcile(42, processing, [this](const server_scx_state_v2 * event) { events.push_back(*event); });
+    }
+    void check() const {
+        uint64_t sequence = 0;
+        for (const auto & event : events) {
+            CHECK(event.version == 2 && event.run_id == 42 && event.reserved == 0);
+            CHECK(event.sequence == ++sequence);
+            CHECK(event.active <= 1 && event.phase <= 3);
+            CHECK(event.active || event.phase == 0);
+        }
+    }
+};
+
+static void test_lifecycle() {
+    recorder r;
+    bool processing = true;
+    int settled = 0;
+    auto reconcile = [&]() { r.reconcile(processing); };
+    auto clear = [&]() { ++settled; r.reconcile(false); };
+    r.publish(2);
+    {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        CHECK(r.events.size() == 1);
+    }
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 1);
+    {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        processing = false;
+    }
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 2);
+    r.publish(2);
+    processing = true;
+    try {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        throw 1;
+    } catch (int) {}
+    CHECK(settled == 1 && r.events.size() == 4 && r.events.back().active == 0);
+    r.publish(1);
+    clear();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 6);
+    r.publish(2);
+    CHECK(r.events.back().sequence == 7);
+    clear();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 8);
+    r.check();
+}
+
+static void test_early_return() {
+    recorder r;
+    r.publish(2);
+    auto iteration = [&]() {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard([&]() { r.reconcile(false); }, [&]() { std::abort(); });
+        return;
+    };
+    iteration();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 2 && r.events.back().active == 0);
+    r.check();
+}
+
+static void test_ranges() {
+    recorder r;
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(0, 0, 0) == 0);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 1) == 0);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 0, 0) == 1);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(0, 3, 0) == 2);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 0) == 3);
+    r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 0));
+    r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 0, 0));
+    CHECK(!r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(2, 0, 0)));
+    r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(0, 3, 0));
+    r.reconcile(false);
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 4);
+    r.check();
+}
+
+int main() {
+    test_lifecycle();
+    test_ranges();
+    test_early_return();
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, version) == 0, "v1 version");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, run_id) == 8, "v1 run_id");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, call_id) == 16, "v1 call_id");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, retry) == 24, "v1 retry");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, phase) == 32, "v1 phase");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, profile) == 40, "v1 profile");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, n_prefill) == 48, "v1 n_prefill");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, n_decode) == 56, "v1 n_decode");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, n_unknown) == 64, "v1 n_unknown");
+    static_assert(offsetof(server_scx_event, result) == 72, "v1 result");
+    recorder repeated;
+    CHECK(!repeated.reconcile(false));
+    for (int i = 0; i < 100; ++i) {
+        CHECK(repeated.publish(2) == (i == 0));
+        CHECK(!repeated.reconcile(true));
+    }
+    CHECK(repeated.reconcile(false));
+    CHECK(repeated.events.size() == 2);
+    CHECK(repeated.events[0].phase == 2 && repeated.events[0].active == 1);
+    CHECK(repeated.events[1].phase == 0 && repeated.events[1].active == 0);
+    repeated.check();
+
+    recorder transitions;
+    for (uint32_t phase : { 1u, 2u, 2u, 3u, 2u }) { transitions.publish(phase); }
+    transitions.reconcile(false);
+    CHECK(transitions.events.size() == 5);
+    transitions.check();
+
+    recorder lifecycle;
+    CHECK(lifecycle.publish(0));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.events.back().active == 1 && lifecycle.events.back().phase == 0);
+    CHECK(!lifecycle.reconcile(true));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.reconcile(false));
+    CHECK(!lifecycle.reconcile(false));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.publish(2));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.reconcile(false));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.publish(1));
+    CHECK(lifecycle.events.back().sequence == 5);
+    CHECK(lifecycle.reconcile(false));
+    lifecycle.check();
+
+    server_scx_state_publisher disabled;
+    CHECK(!disabled.publish(0, 2, true, [](const server_scx_state_v2 *) { std::abort(); }));
+    int pinned_events = 0;
+    auto pinned_emit = [&](const server_scx_state_v2 * event) {
+        CHECK(event->run_id == 42 && event->sequence == uint64_t(++pinned_events));
+    };
+    server_scx_state_publisher pinned;
+    CHECK(pinned.publish(42, 2, true, pinned_emit));
+    CHECK(!pinned.publish(43, 1, true, pinned_emit));
+    CHECK(!pinned.idle(43, pinned_emit));
+    CHECK(pinned.idle(42, pinned_emit));
+    CHECK(pinned_events == 2);
+    std::puts("SCX state publisher: counts, active UNKNOWN, reconciliation, resume sequence and ABI passed");
+}

+# SCX state notification validation
+
+Candidate date: 2026-10-03. Provider: personal `hsju2021/llama.cpp-fork`, branch `codex/scx-state-notification`, based on `64f4f972a2758d3a730ce78f92aaa05406de40a0`. Scheduler: the paired `llama-scheduler` checkout based on `ffc03c8`. Changes are uncommitted. The M11/M11R provider pin and archived results remain unchanged.
+
+## Implemented scope
+
+- Server modes `off|trace|state`, order-independent option validation, and run-ID-only trace compatibility.
+- Unchanged 80-byte v1 server ABI plus the separate 32-byte v2 state ABI, with size and all field offsets asserted on both sides.
+- Transition suppression, actual submitted-view classification, retained synchronization, and execution-loop cleanup for idle, cancellation, errors, sleep, and exit.
+- Worker endpoint removal with the final graph barrier preserved.
+- Matching scheduler attachment modes, bounded TGID state, run/sequence validation, failure invalidation, process-instance cleanup, and mode-aware reports.
+- A separate candidate acceptance path, including graceful completion and termination during active DECODE, without changing the historical trace provider pin.
+
+Scheduling policy and compute-profile routing are unchanged. The state interval includes sampling and server processing; it is not a v1 compute interval. No performance improvement is claimed.
+
+## Local evidence
+
+Validation runs in an isolated Linux-filesystem source copy under `/home/hs/scx-state-validation`, using WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`. Build tools were extracted into that task directory without system installation or elevated commands. Raw logs, build options, symbol checks, source hashes, and reproduction scripts are retained in `results/scx-state-notification-20261003-local/` in the provider worktree.
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Trace ON, OpenMP ON server build | PASS, clean rebuild |
+| Trace OFF, OpenMP ON server build | PASS |
+| Trace ON, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Trace OFF, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Provider CTest: argument parser, compute profile, state publisher, enabled-build synchronization fixture | 14/14 passed across the four builds |
+| Small CPU ADD/MUL f32 backend checks | 100/100 per build, 400/400 total |
+| ELF symbols in all four builds | PASS: worker symbols absent; v1/v2 server markers present only with trace enabled |
+| Scheduler userspace and BPF compilation with `-Werror` | PASS, compile evidence only |
+| Scheduler Python suites: instrumentation, M11, M11R, state, M10B, validation | 64 cases: 62 passed, 2 skipped |
+| Full scheduler `make check` | Environment gate: selected-child shell test stops because `/sys/kernel/sched_ext/state` is absent |
+| Python/shell syntax and both repository whitespace checks | PASS |
+
+The two skipped cases require separate historical provider checkouts: the legacy socket producer and the fixed M11 semantic source. Current provider ABI and publisher checks run independently in the C++ fixtures. The shell gate expects a native sched_ext state file; the WSL launcher reports that the file is missing. It was not bypassed or treated as native success.
+
+The final ELF audit detected an old worker symbol in the initially reused ON/OpenMP build. Preserved source timestamps had allowed an object from the baseline to remain. That variant was rebuilt with `--clean-first`; its tests and symbols were checked again. The other three variants were fresh builds. Final source SHA-256 checks match every changed code/test file to the validated Linux copy.
+
+The BPF compilation uses the external sched-ext x86 `vmlinux-v6.18-rc4-g6146a0f1dfae.h` fixture from scx commit `e37ab1fd7ec09505c33beaefdc128bab2d582660`, and a Linux v6.17 scheduler UAPI fixture. These are recorded compile inputs, not the target kernel's BTF or proof of verifier compatibility.
+
+Executable fixtures exercise production publication, phase reduction, lifecycle guards, synchronization, BPF handlers, map/read failures, run and sequence rejection, active UNKNOWN, real-child pidfd cleanup, exit/update races, and report acceptance. They verify two notifications for 100 repeated DECODE calls followed by IDLE, and five notifications for PREFILL/DECODE/DECODE/MIXED/DECODE/IDLE. Actual server token extraction, slot completion/cancellation, model unload, and loop integration were source-reviewed; model-backed lifecycle runs remain pending.
+
+Registration cleanup also exercises 127 successive process identities, same-PID reuse, and deletion failures. The last inactive state is retained for reporting, then reclaimed when the next registration starts, so completed processes do not fill the bounded map.
+
+## Manual checkpoint
+
+The paired scheduler's `docs/LLAMA_PHASE.md` contains the exact native build and runtime commands. Its `AGENTS.md` requires explicit approval before `sudo` or sched_ext loading. No kernel load, uprobe attachment, SCHED_EXT workload, model inference, or performance trial was executed locally.
+
+On the intended native host, verify the selected Ryzen 5 5600G / 48 GB machine, target BTF/UAPI, actual ELF paths, and build options. Run the old trace acceptance and the new state acceptance separately. The controlled state path requires exactly three applied transitions and sequence 3 for normal completion. The abnormal path adds PREFILL and DECODE from a second request, then requires sequence 5 plus evidence that termination invalidated active DECODE. Zero delivery, per-call DECODE publication, sequence gaps, and diagnostic failures fail acceptance.
+
+Then agree on regression thresholds and run matched trace-disabled, runtime-off, trace, and state timing trials with fixed policy and instrumentation. Keep hit-count diagnostics separate from timed runs and preserve raw SSE grouped events. Live reattachment, resynchronization after loader restart, synchronization removal, and policy changes remain deferred.

+# SCX state notification validation
+
+Candidate date: 2026-10-03. Provider: personal `hsju2021/llama.cpp-fork`, branch `codex/scx-state-notification`, based on `64f4f972a2758d3a730ce78f92aaa05406de40a0`. Scheduler: the paired `llama-scheduler` checkout based on `ffc03c8`. Changes are uncommitted. The M11/M11R provider pin and archived results remain unchanged.
+
+## Implemented scope
+
+- Server modes `off|trace|state`, order-independent option validation, and run-ID-only trace compatibility.
+- Unchanged 80-byte v1 server ABI plus the separate 32-byte v2 state ABI, with size and all field offsets asserted on both sides.
+- Transition suppression, actual submitted-view classification, retained synchronization, and execution-loop cleanup for idle, cancellation, errors, sleep, and exit.
+- Worker endpoint removal with the final graph barrier preserved.
+- Matching scheduler attachment modes, bounded TGID state, run/sequence validation, failure invalidation, process-instance cleanup, and mode-aware reports.
+- A separate candidate acceptance path, including graceful completion and termination during active DECODE, without changing the historical trace provider pin.
+
+Scheduling policy and compute-profile routing are unchanged. The state interval includes sampling and server processing; it is not a v1 compute interval. No performance improvement is claimed.
+
+## Local evidence
+
+Validation runs in an isolated Linux-filesystem source copy under `/home/hs/scx-state-validation`, using WSL Ubuntu 24.04 with kernel `6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2`. Build tools were extracted into that task directory without system installation or elevated commands. Raw logs, build options, symbol checks, source hashes, and reproduction scripts are retained in `results/scx-state-notification-20261003-local/` in the provider worktree.
+
+| Check | Result |
+| --- | --- |
+| Trace ON, OpenMP ON server build | PASS, clean rebuild |
+| Trace OFF, OpenMP ON server build | PASS |
+| Trace ON, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Trace OFF, native threadpool server build | PASS |
+| Provider CTest: argument parser, compute profile, state publisher, enabled-build synchronization fixture | 14/14 passed across the four builds |
+| Small CPU ADD/MUL f32 backend checks | 100/100 per build, 400/400 total |
+| ELF symbols in all four builds | PASS: worker symbols absent; v1/v2 server markers present only with trace enabled |
+| Scheduler userspace and BPF compilation with `-Werror` | PASS, compile evidence only |
+| Scheduler Python suites: instrumentation, M11, M11R, state, M10B, validation | 64 cases: 62 passed, 2 skipped |
+| Full scheduler `make check` | Environment gate: selected-child shell test stops because `/sys/kernel/sched_ext/state` is absent |
+| Python/shell syntax and both repository whitespace checks | PASS |
+
+The two skipped cases require separate historical provider checkouts: the legacy socket producer and the fixed M11 semantic source. Current provider ABI and publisher checks run independently in the C++ fixtures. The shell gate expects a native sched_ext state file; the WSL launcher reports that the file is missing. It was not bypassed or treated as native success.
+
+The final ELF audit detected an old worker symbol in the initially reused ON/OpenMP build. Preserved source timestamps had allowed an object from the baseline to remain. That variant was rebuilt with `--clean-first`; its tests and symbols were checked again. The other three variants were fresh builds. Final source SHA-256 checks match every changed code/test file to the validated Linux copy.
+
+The BPF compilation uses the external sched-ext x86 `vmlinux-v6.18-rc4-g6146a0f1dfae.h` fixture from scx commit `e37ab1fd7ec09505c33beaefdc128bab2d582660`, and a Linux v6.17 scheduler UAPI fixture. These are recorded compile inputs, not the target kernel's BTF or proof of verifier compatibility.
+
+Executable fixtures exercise production publication, phase reduction, lifecycle guards, synchronization, BPF handlers, map/read failures, run and sequence rejection, active UNKNOWN, real-child pidfd cleanup, exit/update races, and report acceptance. They verify two notifications for 100 repeated DECODE calls followed by IDLE, and five notifications for PREFILL/DECODE/DECODE/MIXED/DECODE/IDLE. Actual server token extraction, slot completion/cancellation, model unload, and loop integration were source-reviewed; model-backed lifecycle runs remain pending.
+
+Registration cleanup also exercises 127 successive process identities, same-PID reuse, and deletion failures. The last inactive state is retained for reporting, then reclaimed when the next registration starts, so completed processes do not fill the bounded map.
+
+## Manual checkpoint
+
+The paired scheduler's `docs/LLAMA_PHASE.md` contains the exact native build and runtime commands. Its `AGENTS.md` requires explicit approval before `sudo` or sched_ext loading. No kernel load, uprobe attachment, SCHED_EXT workload, model inference, or performance trial was executed locally.
+
+On the intended native host, verify the selected Ryzen 5 5600G / 48 GB machine, target BTF/UAPI, actual ELF paths, and build options. Run the old trace acceptance and the new state acceptance separately. The controlled state path requires exactly three applied transitions and sequence 3 for normal completion. The abnormal path adds PREFILL and DECODE from a second request, then requires sequence 5 plus evidence that termination invalidated active DECODE. Zero delivery, per-call DECODE publication, sequence gaps, and diagnostic failures fail acceptance.
+
+Then agree on regression thresholds and run matched trace-disabled, runtime-off, trace, and state timing trials with fixed policy and instrumentation. Keep hit-count diagnostics separate from timed runs and preserve raw SSE grouped events. Live reattachment, resynchronization after loader restart, synchronization removal, and policy changes remain deferred.

+#include "../tools/server/server-scx.h"
+
+#include <cstdio>
+#include <cstdlib>
+#include <vector>
+
+#define CHECK(condition) do { if (!(condition)) { std::fprintf(stderr, "%s:%d: %s\n", __FILE__, __LINE__, #condition); std::abort(); } } while (0)
+
+struct recorder {
+    server_scx_state_publisher publisher;
+    std::vector<server_scx_state_v2> events;
+
+    bool publish(uint32_t phase) {
+        return publisher.publish(42, phase, true, [this](const server_scx_state_v2 * event) { events.push_back(*event); });
+    }
+    bool reconcile(bool processing) {
+        return publisher.reconcile(42, processing, [this](const server_scx_state_v2 * event) { events.push_back(*event); });
+    }
+    void check() const {
+        uint64_t sequence = 0;
+        for (const auto & event : events) {
+            CHECK(event.version == 2 && event.run_id == 42 && event.reserved == 0);
+            CHECK(event.sequence == ++sequence);
+            CHECK(event.active <= 1 && event.phase <= 3);
+            CHECK(event.active || event.phase == 0);
+        }
+    }
+};
+
+static void test_lifecycle() {
+    recorder r;
+    bool processing = true;
+    int settled = 0;
+    auto reconcile = [&]() { r.reconcile(processing); };
+    auto clear = [&]() { ++settled; r.reconcile(false); };
+    r.publish(2);
+    {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        CHECK(r.events.size() == 1);
+    }
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 1);
+    {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        processing = false;
+    }
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 2);
+    r.publish(2);
+    processing = true;
+    try {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard(reconcile, clear);
+        throw 1;
+    } catch (int) {}
+    CHECK(settled == 1 && r.events.size() == 4 && r.events.back().active == 0);
+    r.publish(1);
+    clear();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 6);
+    r.publish(2);
+    CHECK(r.events.back().sequence == 7);
+    clear();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 8);
+    r.check();
+}
+
+static void test_early_return() {
+    recorder r;
+    r.publish(2);
+    auto iteration = [&]() {
+        server_scx_reconcile_scope guard([&]() { r.reconcile(false); }, [&]() { std::abort(); });
+        return;
+    };
+    iteration();
+    CHECK(r.events.size() == 2 && r.events.back().active == 0);
+    r.check();
+}
+
+static void test_ranges() {
+    recorder r;
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(0, 0, 0) == 0);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 1) == 0);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 0, 0) == 1);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(0, 3, 0) == 2);
+    CHECK(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 0) == 3);
+    r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 3, 0));
+    r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(4, 0, 0));
+    CHECK(!r.publish(server_scx_classify_phase(2, 0, 0)));
